title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: elliptic curves E/S with 2 invertible on S. Earlier pages introduce several objects. J is the finite étale S-scheme of degree 3 of nonzero 2-torsion points. Σ_J is the conic bundle E/{±1}, a P^1-bundle over S. D_J ⊂ Σ_J is the image of J, three of the four branch points of the double cover E → Σ_J; the fourth branch point is the image of the origin. The earlier pages also define a 'Legendre' pinning (31) and a classification of 'exceptional/marginal' curves, Grothendieck's own vocabulary. The previous page shows that a Legendre-type datum alone does not give a rigid problem: objects still have automorphisms, essentially [-1].

This page fixes that. Combine the Legendre pinning k with a 'Jacobi pinning of level 2' u. Here u (35) is a trivialisation J ≅ {0,1,∞}_S, i.e. an ordering of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. Equivalently (36), u is an isomorphism Σ_J ≅ P^1_S carrying D_J onto the divisor {0}+{1}+{∞}. This is equivalent because P^1 with three ordered marked points is rigid. The pair (k,u) is called the Legendre–Jacobi pinning of level 2.

Claim: the fibred category (stack) of elliptic curves with such a pinning is rigid. It is equivalent to the category of pairs (t, α):
- t is a section of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It is the position of the image of the origin, i.e. the Legendre λ / cross-ratio.
- α is a section of μ_4^* (primitive 4th roots of unity). The machine transcription's O_S^* is a misreading; the next page confirms the answer.

Hence the moduli problem is represented by the scheme U_{0,3} × μ_4^* (37). Over Z[1/2] this is Spec Z[1/2, i][λ, 1/(λ(1−λ))].

Why this is plausible. The stack of curves with only an ordering of 2-torsion is Y(2) ≅ U_{0,3} × Bμ_2, the μ_2-gerbe coming from [-1]. The extra Legendre datum k is a μ_2-torsor on which [-1] acts nontrivially. Its universal space is μ_4^* = Spec Z[1/2][i], a nontrivial μ_2-torsor over Spec Z[1/2], with α ↦ −α. This kills the gerbe. The universal curve is the double cover of P^1 branched at 0, 1, ∞, t, normalised by α.

The next page builds on this. It computes the line bundle Δ_E / Π_0 on the universal base. It uses that over μ_4^* (where √−1 exists) the conic bundle Q_0 becomes trivial. It then proposes to study the actions (of S_3, Galois and μ_2) on U_{0,3} × μ_4^* and on Π_0. The goal is evidently an explicit presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a quotient of a rigid scheme U_{0,3} × μ_4^* by a finite group (scheme) of order about 12. This fits the 1980–82 'Lego/Teichmüller tower' programme centred on M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and Galois actions.
errors: Not a mathematical error, but no proof is given on this page. The equivalence with pairs (t, α) presupposes that the Legendre pinning (31) contributes exactly a μ_4^*-torsor on which [-1] acts by α ↦ −α. That must be checked against the definition on earlier pages.
The line 'α une section de O_S^*' in the machine transcription would give U_{0,3} × G_m, which is inconsistent with (37) on the next page. The image reads μ_4^*.

ideas.what: Level-2 structure (ordering of 2-torsion) identified with an isomorphism E/±1 ≅ P^1 sending branch points to 0,1,∞; λ-line U_{0,3} as moduli
ideas.modern_name: Legendre family / Y(2) ≅ P^1−{0,1,∞} (coarse), stack U_{0,3}×Bμ_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre, Jacobi; modern stack form folklore (Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (M_{1,1}, M_{0,4} in the Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Rigidification of the level-2 moduli stack by an extra 'Legendre' datum, giving the fine moduli scheme U_{0,3} × μ_4^*
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of the μ_2-gerbe Y(2) → U_{0,3} via a μ_2-torsor; presentation M_{1,1}[1/2] = [scheme / finite group]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Analogous presentations M_{1,1}[1/2] ≅ [M(2)/GL_2(Z/2)] appear e.g. in Stojanoska's Tmf(2) work (2012); the μ_4^* form is not standard

ideas.what: Conic bundle Q_0 becomes trivial over μ_4^* (√−1 available), giving Π_0 ≅ O(1) (next page)
ideas.modern_name: splitting of a Brauer class / conic by adjoining i

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit rigid atlas U_{0,3}×μ_4^* for elliptic curves over Z[1/2] with Legendre–Jacobi level-2 pinning. He then announces (next page) the study of the actions of the change-of-pinning group on this scheme and on the line bundle Π_0. In effect this is an explicit Z[1/2]-presentation of M_{1,1} as a quotient of U_{0,3}×μ_4^* by a finite group, with arithmetic (μ_4^*/Galois) content built in. It is a slightly unusual variant of known presentations.
missed.quote: La catégorie fibrée des courbes elliptiques munies d'un tel épinglage est alors rigide, et équivalente à celle définie par les couples (t, α), où t est une section de U_{0,3}, α une section de μ_4^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. Equivalent presentations (Legendre/Tmf(2), GL_2(Z/2)-quotients) are standard in stable homotopy and moduli texts. The μ_4^* rigidification could give a tidy Galois-equivariant model relevant to the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) on π_1(M_{1,1}) vs π_1(M_{0,4}), but this is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: Competent working out of the level-2 Legendre moduli and a rigidification giving U_{0,3}×μ_4^*. The ideas are classical or folklore; only the specific μ_4^* rigidification and the 'Legendre–Jacobi pinning' terminology are idiosyncratic, and nothing seems absent from the literature in substance.
transcription_corrections: 'où t est une section de U_{0,1}' should read 'U_{0,3}'.
'α une section de O_S^*' should read 'α une section de μ_4^*' (consistent with (37) on the next page).
'(35) est J ≃ {0,1,∞}_S' should read 'où u : J ≃ {0,1,∞}_S (35) est une trivialisation de J'.
'i.e. une bijection[?]' is more likely 'i.e. un isom.' introducing (36).
'il est loisible[?]' is uncertain; the word looks like 'naturel' or 'utile'.
Last line: 'donc la catégorie champ[?] une' is probably 'donc la catégorie [fibrée/en] groupoïdes envisagée', continuing onto the next page.
